title: Basic Shell Commands
subtitle: man, navigation, files, env, and pagers — flip to reveal meaning

cards.meaning: Main UNIX help; argument is normally a program, utility, or function
cards.notes: Default searches all available sections. Prefer man on a server over a browser

Keyword search — commands whose description contains the word (like apropos)
Short one-line description of ls (like whatis)
User commands (ls, cat)
System calls
Library functions (printf)
File formats (fstab, passwd file format)
Admin commands (useradd)
Same ideas as less — arrows/j k to move, /pattern to search, q to quit
GNU information pages — often longer and hyperlinked; man is the Unix default to try first
cards.notes: DevOps default: man, then -k if you forgot the name

cards.meaning: Full description of info itself
Long format + all entries (do not skip names starting with .)
cards.notes: -l = long; -a = all (dotfiles). Ops almost always wants this

cards.meaning: Long format + human-readable sizes (1K, 234M, 2G)
Long format, sort by time, newest first
Long format, sort by Size (largest first), human-readable sizes

Search path for cd (like PATH for directories); : -separated; null entry means .; ignored if dest begins with /
Go to filesystem root
Go to parent of the current directory
Go to user’s home directory (same idea as $HOME)
Previous directory (toggles back); also prints the path it landed on

Create an empty directory
Set mode as in chmod (not a=rwx minus umask)
Make parent dirs as needed; no error if they already exist

cards.meaning: Copy directories recursively (with all subdirectories)

cards.meaning: Same as --preserve=mode,ownership,timestamps
Keep attributes (default: mode, ownership, timestamps); extra: context, links, xattr, all
Prompt before overwrite (overrides a previous -n)
Move or rename a file or directory (rename = move in the same parent)
Prompt before overwrite
Backup each existing destination before overwrite

cards.meaning: Backup suffix instead of the default ~
Move only if SOURCE is newer than destination, or destination is missing
Display a file, or concatenate files into one

cards.meaning: Remove an empty directory only
Remove (unlink) files, or directories with -r

cards.meaning: Ignore missing files; never prompt
Remove directories and their contents recursively

Overwrite so recovery is harder (stronger destruction than plain rm)
No args: print environment. Or run a program in a custom environment without changing the current shell
Print all or named environment variables
Print everything — environment, shell variables, and shell functions

cards.meaning: Delete shell and environment variables
Turn a name into an environment variable inherited by children

cards.meaning: Old pager — can scroll down but not up
cards.notes: Some small embedded systems have more but not less

cards.meaning: Pager that can scroll both ways (written because more could not go backwards); prefer on a normal server
cards.notes: less is more. q to quit

cards.meaning: Search forward (regex); starts at the first displayed line; N defaults to 1

Repeat previous search same direction / reverse direction
Print the first 10 lines of a file by default
First K lines instead of 10
All but the last K lines of each file
Print the last 10 lines by default
Last K lines instead of 10
Output starting at line K through the end
